memory_candidates.content: update-phase-status.sh's phase-heading regex replacement can corrupt a heading whose title contains a literal `[` (e.g. a plan phase titled with a code-formatted `dependencies[]`) -- it truncated everything from the first `[` onward, eating the rest of the title and the trailing status marker. If a plan phase title must contain literal brackets, verify the heading text after every update-phase-status.sh call (grep '^### Phase' the plan file) rather than assuming the marker-only edit was clean.

In this orchestrator codebase, skill-orchestrate-hard's multi-task mode (Stage 0: 'if multi_task_mode true, use base multi-task stages') delegates its ENTIRE Stage MT-1 through MT-5 runtime -- schema field declarations, per-cycle accumulators, and postflight read/report/write -- to skill-orchestrate/SKILL.md. The hard twin's own '## Multi-Task Mode' section only re-transcribes specific admission-gate/redeploy-checkpoint BEHAVIORAL prose (for documentation-reinforcement reasons, since a bare 'same as base' pointer previously failed to carry a mechanism forward). When adding a new Stage MT-1 accumulator field (e.g. a new observation ledger) for a base-skill mechanism, do NOT duplicate the schema declaration in the hard twin -- add a short 'Accumulator note' there instead, pointing back to the base skill, matching how defer_ledger and forward_progress_violated are already documented.

check-extension-docs.sh's Rule R validates a maintained line_count field in agent-system/extensions/<ext>/index-entries.json against each indexed context/patterns doc's ACTUAL file line count. Growing an existing indexed doc file (adding a section, appending prose) without updating its index-entries.json line_count entry introduces a new doc-lint FAIL that looks like unrelated drift but is actually caused by that same edit. After any edit that changes an indexed doc file's line count, grep index-entries.json for that file's path and update line_count to match `wc -l` before considering the doc-lint gate clean.
